reviewed_by: Automated static review, 2026-10-23: Binary Ninja MCP, Radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe against engine/src/retail/config/input_remap.cpp and the linked candidate 0x0040C7C0.
scope: The complete 0x004037C0 body: action-count and action-slot reads, the remap-slot arithmetic, the three argument stores, the action-slot increment, the six-dword result block and the returned destination pointer. The 0x004B8A20 frame reader is modelled by the port's QvmFrameView and is not re-implemented.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja and Radare2 independently recover one function entry at 0x004037C0 with a one-node, zero-edge graph (recorded similarity 1.000); angr CFGFast recovers the same exact entry and finds no unresolved jumps. The candidate entry is GOInRemap at 0x0040C7C0 in build-clean-win32/igi1.exe, called once from decode_input_config at 0x0040F302.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Stack arithmetic at the retail prologue reads the destination pointer at [esp+0x28], leaves [esp+0x2C] unused and reads the script frame at [esp+0x30], so the retail shape is cdecl(destination, unused, frame) returning the destination in EAX. The candidate extern "C" entry takes exactly (std::uint32_t* result, std::int32_t unused, void* qvm_context) and returns std::uint32_t*. The engine decoder has no QVM result buffer, so the header's single-argument overload supplies a static host destination and forwards; that adapter is an engine-boundary adaptation, documented as such.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The candidate uses the retail literals: action table base 0x00BC2358, action count 0x00BC2380, 345-dword action stride, (count - 1) * 115 + action remap slot, remap base 0x00BC25BC, 3-dword remap stride, 0x3FFFFFFF argument-2 mask, six-dword result block and the script type descriptor 0x00567C74 at block dword 4 (byte +0x10).

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: The candidate reads the count and the action slot, writes the three remap dwords, increments the same action slot the call read, and copies six dwords to the caller's destination. It preserves the retail table bases and strides, including the fact that the action records and the remap region overlap (the action record for count 1 starts at 0x00BC28BC, inside the 0x00BC25BC remap region); only the low action-record dwords are read, so the overlap is harmless.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: Retail calls the frame reader 0x004B8A20 three times with frame and indices 0, 1, 2; the candidate reads the same three words through the QvmFrameView the decoder already fills. The only stores are the three remap dwords, the action-slot increment and the six-dword destination block. Retail writes neither block dword 1 nor dword 5; the candidate zeroes both deterministically, recorded as a deviation.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Retail has no branch after the prologue and no error path: rep movsd leaves arg1 in EAX and the routine returns it. The candidate returns the destination pointer it was given, and the differential confirms the relation return == destination on all nine cases. Argument 2 is masked with 0x3FFFFFFF before the store in both.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: The body performs no floating-point arithmetic. The 0x00567C74 value is an opaque script type descriptor stamped into the result block, not a float.

review_findings: The action slot is incremented at 0x00403824-0x0040382C from the same address esi = &InputRemap_ActionTable[count] that supplied the action, not from InputRemap_ActionCount; the caller increments the count independently, so there is no double increment.

The six-dword block is copied to the arg1 destination with rep movsd x6 and the destination is returned in EAX; the old candidate returned entry[2] & 0x3FFFFFFF and performed neither operation, which this revision fixes.
Retail leaves block dwords 1 and 5 unwritten (stack residue). The port writes zero for determinism; the differential records only dwords 0, 2, 3 and 4 as compared observables.
The retail has no capacity check on count or slot; the host port also performs none inside the native. The engine's action_table_capacity bound lives in the decoder, not in this native.
No paired retail/candidate runtime capture exists. This review authorizes STRUCTURALLY_VERIFIED only, not behavioural or runtime equivalence.
limits: The engine decoder calls the single-argument overload with a host static destination; retail's destination is the caller's QVM buffer. The relation and block contents are compared, not the pointer value.
The 0x004B8A20 frame reader is replaced by the port's QvmFrameView; the differential stubs that reader to return case arguments, so the reader itself is not verified here.
Retail's uninitialised block dwords 1 and 5 become deterministic zeros in the port.
No paired retail/candidate runtime capture exists; status is capped at STRUCTURALLY_VERIFIED.
